answer: Graduated identity resists sybil attacks by making trust expensive and slow. A new agent must stake collateral and finish a probation of honest work before it earns voting weight, so a factory that wants a nebula of fake accounts pays a full stake and survives weeks of audit for every single one. Legitimate users pass the same narrow jetty cheaply because they register once, while bulk farms burn real capital per identity — their timber is spent the moment an auditor catches the clone pattern and slashes the bond. Spend scales with scale, and honesty stays the cheaper route.
